decisions.decision: Use the Ollama OpenAI-compatible speech endpoint with bounded PCM, then wrap and transcode the complete result.
decisions.why: It avoids Ollama WAV placeholder lengths and preserves the service complete response, speed, format, timeout, and output bounds.
decisions.rejected: Returning Ollama WAV directly or introducing client-facing MP3 streaming before those guarantees are proven.

decisions.decision: Treat phonon:31m-en and phonon:40m-de as candidates, not runtime defaults, and require explicit reviewed model and voice approval before availability.
decisions.why: Official pages identify the language fit and different licenses, while exact asset identity, voice terms, target compatibility, and use approval remain open.
decisions.rejected: Unreviewed hard-coded tags or placeholder voice IDs.

decisions.decision: Leave the Phonon endpoint unset by default and initially accept only a verified loopback origin without redirects or ambient proxies.
decisions.why: Ollama local speech is unauthenticated and the deployment path is not yet verified.
decisions.rejected: Accepting arbitrary remote origins or assuming container-to-host networking is trusted.

decisions.decision: Split client text at safe boundaries under the documented 4096-character API limit and preserve all segments under shared request and output bounds.
decisions.why: The API does not perform CLI long-input splitting, and rejecting or truncating such requests would violate the feature requirements.
decisions.rejected: Relying on API truncation or sending oversized requests.

plan.summary: Planned a disabled-by-default Phonon integration with bounded PCM conversion and explicit asset and network gates.
plan.key_finding: The official speech API supports PCM and named voices but caps each input at 4096 characters and does not provide speed or MP3.

approach: Use a small standard-library adapter behind the existing engine registry. Keep model and voice assets unavailable until an approved record and trusted local endpoint are configured; preserve the existing complete-response conversion path.

FR-001.title: The replacement MUST remove Fish as a selectable engine and MUST NOT require Fish assets or services for the speech service to start or become ready.

FR-002.title: The replacement MUST provide Phonon speech for English and German when the approved model, voice, and target environment support the requested language.

FR-003.title: The replacement MUST retain native macOS `say` as an available speech option where the host supports it.

FR-004.title: The replacement MUST preserve established authentication, speed control, voice selection, MP3/WAV output, response metadata, and the existing encoded-request size safeguard. It MUST NOT retain a fixed 5,000-unit text limit.

FR-005.title: The replacement MUST handle text beyond a selected model's per-input capacity by dividing it into supported segments and returning a complete result that preserves the text's order and content, subject to existing request, time, and audio-output safeguards.

FR-006.title: The replacement SHOULD stream MP3 audio to the user when it can preserve the established response behavior, bounded output, cancellation, timeout, and safe-error guarantees. If it cannot, it MUST retain the current complete-response behavior and MUST NOT claim that client-facing streaming is supported.

FR-007.title: Successful responses MUST continue to identify the engine that actually generated the audio and preserve the existing response metadata required by clients.

FR-008.title: The service MUST retain its existing user authentication. The unauthenticated Phonon service MUST remain reachable only over a verified, trusted path and MUST NOT be exposed beyond the separately approved network boundary.

FR-009.title: Errors and logs MUST NOT disclose speech text, credentials, or private host configuration.

FR-010.title: Exact Phonon model and voice assets MUST NOT be used until their source, terms, provenance, and compatibility with the stated private, non-commercial intended use have been reviewed.

FR-011.title: The replacement MUST report Phonon as unavailable when its required model or service is unavailable; it MUST NOT silently route a selected Phonon request to native macOS speech.

FR-012.title: The replacement MUST NOT require a predefined quality threshold before productive use. If the requester reports after productive use that expectations are not met, a dedicated follow-up MUST be created; this does not waive rights, platform, privacy, or operational gates.
FR-012.assumes: No post-use report has been made; create a dedicated follow-up if one occurs. No pre-use quality threshold is added.
